hero.oneLiner: Independent, home-grown Indian alternative asset management company operating under the "Gaja Capital" brand, acting as investment manager to India-focused Category II and Category I AIFs and as advisor to offshore funds, with 20 years of vintage in the mid-market private equity segment.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Independent, home-grown Indian alternative asset management company operating under the "Gaja Capital" brand, acting as investment manager to India-focused Category II and Category I AIFs and as advisor to offshore funds, with 20 years of vintage in the mid-market private equity segment.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manages and advises India-focused alternative investment funds (the Gaja Capital Funds — Fund II formed 2007, Fund III 2015 and Fund IV 2021) plus a newly launched Secondaries Fund, providing growth capital to mid-market Portfolio Companies in EEE, financial services, consumer and digital technology. It earns income from three streams — Management Fee (a function of fund size, generally fixed at two percent in proportion to the size of the fund), Carried Interest (a function of a fund's net IRR) and Income from Sponsor Commitment (a function of a fund's gross MOIC) — all of which are received in their entirety by the Company rather than shared with individuals. Its limited partners are institutional investors, sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, insurers, family offices and HNIs/UHNIs spread across more than 20 countries; investors in the Offer become shareholders of the AMC entity and not investors in the funds.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: There is no physical supply chain; the relevant integration is vertical integration of the fund-management value chain and full capture of fund economics into the listed entity. (1) Economic integration: 'All the income generated from the funds managed and advised by us, across the three income streams, is received in its entirety by us. Our objective has been to capture the economic value generated by the funds managed and advised by us within our Company, with the goal of enhancing our enterprise value and strengthening our balance sheet.' No Carried Interest is allocated to any individual — 'all the Carried Interest generated across our Gaja Capital Funds is attributable to our Company without any specific allocation to any individual'. (2) Structural integration: the Company acts as investment manager to the India-domiciled AIF constituents while its own subsidiary Gaja Advisors Ltd, Mauritius acts as investment manager to the Mauritius-domiciled constituent funds, and Eastgate Secondaries Advisor LLP (in which the Company holds an investment) will manage the proposed Secondaries Fund; operations run through seven subsidiaries (four Indian, one overseas, two overseas step-down). (3) Backward integration into distribution (fund-raising): 'We have traditionally relied on our network of investors to raise funds for the Gaja Capital Funds while keeping the proportion of funds raised through third-party distributors low' — three distributors used in Fiscal 2024 and none in Fiscal 2025 or Fiscal 2026. (4) Balance-sheet integration into the funds: sponsor commitments substantially above the SEBI AIF Regulations threshold (Rs 2,740.00 million, 6.41% of total fund size as of March 31, 2026, against a prescribed 2.5% of corpus or Rs 50.00 million, whichever is lower), the past warehousing of an investment in a portfolio company for Fund IV on the Company's own balance sheet, and investment of balance-sheet capital in third-party funds to bolster deal flow. (5) Forward integration into the Portfolio Companies via the four-professional Operating Team's 'invest-and-collaborate' model operating at three engagement levels (board participation; strategic areas; operational support), with board representation in nearly all Portfolio Companies. (6) Outsourced functions are explicitly limited: 'We work with professional firms for support across accounting, legal and valuation related matters'; fund administration is staffed by 7 contractual personnel. Headcount as of March 31, 2026: 37 total — 23 permanent (Core Team 15, comprising Investment Team 10, Operating Team 4, Investor Relations 1; Finance Team 3; IT 1; Administrative staff 3; Compliance Team 1) and 14 contractual (Fund Administration 7; Housekeeping and Security 7), plus an Operating Advisors Group of two former CXOs. Attrition of total employees: 3 / 1 / 3 (13.33% / 4.76% / 16.22%) in Fiscal 2026 / 2025 / 2024, with nil attrition among Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management in all three fiscals.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Ability to establish new and larger funds — Management Fee is calculated on the overall capital committed to a fund and is generally fixed at two percent in proportion to the size of the fund; delays or reductions in future fund sizes would compress the management fee pool.
- Fund investment performance — Carried Interest is proportional to net profits generated by the funds, subject to a minimum IRR threshold, and Income from Sponsor Commitment is a direct function of gross MOIC; the latter was Nil in Fiscal 2025 primarily on account of a fair value loss.
- Income mix shift — Management Fee fell from 72.96% of total income in Fiscal 2024 to 46.65% in Fiscal 2025 and 38.07% in Fiscal 2026 while Carried Interest rose from 17.69% to 52.25% to 47.79%, making income increasingly performance-linked.
- Ability to execute growth strategies — shortfalls in raising, deploying and managing the Secondaries Fund would impact total income and profit after tax in coming years.
- Fund-raising cost discipline — reliance on a proprietary network of advisors, industry participants and existing investors keeps the share of funds raised via distributors low (₹844.92 million raised through distributors in Fiscal 2024); a change in distributor mix or commission structure would pressure profitability.
- Employee cost and retention lever — equity ownership rather than cash compensation keeps employee benefit expenses in a 20–23% band of total income (22.26% Fiscal 2026, 23.16% Fiscal 2025, 20.84% Fiscal 2024) with nil KMP/SMP attrition over three years.
- Operating leverage — cost-to-income ratio of 44.61% in Fiscal 2026 versus 52.28% in Fiscal 2025 and 47.12% in Fiscal 2024, driven by calibrated growth in the employee base (37 personnel across permanent and contractual staff as of March 31, 2026).
- Balance sheet capital usage — Sponsor Commitment, past warehousing of an investment for Fund IV, and investments in third-party funds to bolster deal flow make parts of an otherwise asset-light model capital-intensive.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Drive growth in the enterprise value of the Company through four key value drivers: raising larger funds, delivering better returns from the funds managed and advised, maintaining a higher share of Sponsor Commitment, and keeping fundraising costs lower.
- Capitalize on the growth of the AIF segment and deepen focus on high-growth sectors (EEE, financial services, consumer, digital technology) in the mid-market segment of the Indian economy.
- Continue to focus on delivering sustained growth and investment performance in the flagship private equity strategy, launching new funds with an increasing corpus to drive greater Management Fee, and maintaining higher-than-prescribed sponsor commitment in future funds.
- Leverage expertise to progress on new growth strategies — build a diversified business platform beyond Category II AIFs and offshore private equity funds, including the newly launched Secondaries Fund providing GP solutions.
- Strengthen the employee value proposition to attract and retain talent — ownership-oriented, meritocratic model with equity ownership across senior leadership, continued upskilling and development of a pool of potential leaders.
- Enhance investor reach in India and globally and strengthen industry relationships — deepen ties with existing LPs and build a new investor pool to source capital for future funds.
- Improve margin profile by leveraging operating experience as the business scales further.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion is fund-platform expansion, not physical capacity — the RHP states the business model does not require substantial investment in fixed assets. Three tracks are described. (1) Fund IV: of the ₹1,500.00 million Sponsor Commitment approved by the Board on June 8, 2020, ₹1,125.00 million has been invested and ₹375.00 million remains outstanding as Balance Sponsor Commitment (₹21.55 million to Gaja Capital India Fund 2020 LLP and ₹353.45 million to Gaja Capital India Fund 2021), estimated to be deployed by Fiscals 2027 and 2028, alongside repayment of the ₹195.00 million Bridge Loan Amount availed from ICICI Bank Limited during the three-month period ended June 30, 2026. (2) Proposed Fund V — authorized by Board resolution dated June 13, 2025, trust deed dated June 16, 2025, private placement memorandum application filed with SEBI on June 10, 2026; proposed to be set up in Fiscal 2027 at a proposed size of ₹25,000.00 million in capital commitments, focused on EEE, financial services, consumer and digital technology, with LP marketing and receipt of commitments expected to complete by Fiscal 2027 and deployment over Fiscals 2027, 2028 and 2029. (3) Secondaries Fund — authorized by Board resolution dated February 27, 2025, trust deed dated March 12, 2025; constituent Eastgate Secondaries Fund registered as a Category II AIF (SEBI certificate dated October 17, 2025); proposed size of ₹12,500.00 million in capital commitments, sector agnostic, headed by a chief executive officer with more than 18 years of experience in the global Secondaries market. General corporate purposes include establishment of new office locations.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Well-established alternative AMC with a differentiated business model focused on driving the enterprise value of the Company — all income generated by the Gaja Capital Funds through Management Fees, Carried Interest and Income from Sponsor Commitment is received in its entirety by the Company, with no specific Carried Interest allocation to any individual.
- Independent and home-grown — not sponsored or owned by any financial institution, corporate group or global firm; ownership predominantly held by the leadership team, all of whom developed their careers in India.
- Proven track-record across the Gaja Capital Funds — 28 completed investments (including fully realized) as of March 31, 2026, with a 3.3x average MOIC across the Prior Investments and the Gaja Capital Funds; Fund III and Fund IV rank 1st quartile on both TVPI and IRR versus industry benchmarks.
- Focus on the high-growth Indian alternative asset management industry — AIF commitments grew at approximately 29.2% CAGR between Fiscal 2019 and Fiscal 2026 to ₹16.90 trillion as of March 2026 (Source: Crisil Report).
- Invest-and-collaborate approach — board representation in nearly all Portfolio Companies and a four-professional Operating Team executing scale and transformation plans across product, sales, human resources and financial management, engaged at three defined levels.
- Skin-in-the-game — Sponsor Commitment of approximately ₹2,740.00 million as of March 31, 2026, i.e., 6.41% of the total size of the Gaja Capital Funds, substantially above the SEBI AIF Regulations threshold of 2.5% of fund corpus or ₹50.00 million, whichever is lower (Fund II 5.98%, Fund III 4.38%, Fund IV 8.45%).
- Experienced Promoters and management team — Core Team of 15 professionals (ten-member Investment Team, four-member Operating Team and one investor-relations professional) plus an Operating Advisors Group of two former CXOs; senior leadership averaging 17 years with the Company and nil KMP/SMP attrition in Fiscals 2024, 2025 and 2026.
- Long-standing global LP relationships — 298 Limited Partners as of March 31, 2026 (139 in India, 159 outside India) across more than 20 countries; Fund IV received commitments from 72 domestic LPs.
- Robust financial growth and a strong balance sheet — PAT CAGR of 35.34% between Fiscals 2024 and 2026, PAT Margin improving from 43.04% to 51.94%, borrowings of ₹415.56 million comprising only working capital facilities, and Debt-to-Equity of 0.07 times as of March 31, 2026.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Total income depends on the performance of the funds managed and advised, and the income mix has shifted away from contracted Management Fee toward performance-linked streams — Management Fee was 38.07%, 46.65% and 72.96% of total income in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; Carried Interest is a function of net IRR subject to a minimum threshold and Income from Sponsor Commitment a function of gross MOIC — the latter was Nil in Fiscal 2025 primarily on account of a fair value loss, showing the stream can go to zero in a single year.
- Limited Partner concentration — As of March 31, 2026, the top 10 Limited Partners contributed approximately 63.42% of total commitments in Fund IV (₹10,928.66 million). Failure by these LPs to honour capital calls or a change in their investment behaviour would affect fund performance and the Company's fee base.
- Key-person and small-team dependence — The business rests on three Promoter-Executive Directors and a Core Team of only 15 professionals within a total headcount of 37 permanent and contractual staff as of March 31, 2026; retention is engineered through equity ownership rather than cash compensation, so an inability to retain or recruit skilled personnel would be difficult to substitute.
- Fund-raising risk for the proposed Fund V and the Secondaries Fund — The Net Proceeds are largely earmarked for Sponsor Commitments to funds that are not yet raised. Fund V's private placement memorandum application was filed with SEBI only on June 10, 2026 and there is no assurance the proposed Fund V will be registered or receive approvals within the anticipated timeframe; delay could require variation of the objects of the Offer.
- Regulatory dependence on SEBI AIF Regulations and registrations — The Company operates as manager/sponsor to SEBI-registered AIFs and must maintain continuing sponsor interest; changes to permitted fee structures, sponsor-commitment norms or registration conditions would directly affect all three income streams.
- Outstanding criminal proceedings involving Promoters and a Subsidiary, and investigations touching a former portfolio-linked entity — Gaja Trustee Company Private Limited, Mr. Gopal Jain and Mr. Imran Jafar are involved in FIR No. 0150 (sections 403, 405, 415, 418, 420 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860) filed on behalf of Educomp Learning Private Limited concerning investments in EuroKids International Private Limited, a Fund II portfolio company; the High Court has directed that no coercive steps be taken. Mr. Gopal Jain has separately appeared as a witness before the Serious Fraud Investigation Office and the Central Bureau of Investigation in the Educomp Solutions Limited investigations.
- Broad management discretion over unappraised Net Proceeds — The objects of the Fresh Issue have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution; the deployment schedule across Fiscals 2027–2029 is indicative and management may vary amounts by year, with any variation of objects requiring shareholder approval and an exit opportunity to dissenting shareholders.
- Shareholders of the AMC do not participate in fund returns, and historical fund returns are not indicative — Allottees become shareholders of Gaja Alternative Asset Management Limited and receive no returns, distributions or profits from the funds except to the extent of dividends declared by the Company from its own profits; realisation of Carried Interest is also long-dated given fund life cycles — Fund IV was only 62.00% deployed and unrealized as of March 31, 2026.
